# Servirtium

> Servirtium records the HTTP conversations a test makes and replays them later with no network. The recording ("tape") is canonical, human-readable Markdown, so it can be reviewed in a Git diff and replayed from any language. One engine (servirtium-vcr, written in Aether, shipped as a native library with a C ABI) is wrapped by thin bindings for 30 languages. Current release: {{ site.data.release.tag }}. Nothing is on a language registry: four packaged artifacts and the native libraries are on the GitHub release, and every other language vendors the binding source at the release tag.

Start here:

- [Prompt for a coding agent]({{ site.url }}/agent-prompt/): a ready-to-paste prompt that wraps an existing integration test with Servirtium (record once, commit the tape, play back offline).
- [Everything in one file]({{ site.url }}/llms-full.txt): concepts, features and every language's install steps and quick start.
- [Languages]({{ site.url }}/languages/): table of all 30 bindings, whether each ships an artifact or vendors source, and how to install.
- [Features]({{ site.url }}/features/): what the engine does, how it behaves, examples.
- [Servirtium and OpenAPI]({{ site.url }}/openapi/): exporting tapes to HAR and using existing HAR/OpenAPI tooling.
